title: Seisho Bypass closure expanded again as Typhoon 27 swell kept hitting Kanagawa
summary: The Seisho Bypass disruption became broader than ALAM's earlier update. Sa fourth official report, authorities added a 2.3 km upbound closure from Oiso-nishi IC to Seisho-Ninomiya IC, while the existing downbound and toll-road closures continued. As of the latest official material available this morning, no final reopening notice has been posted.
why_it_matters: If you're driving through Shonan or western Kanagawa, yesterday's earlier closure map is already outdated. More broadly, this is a useful reminder that an offshore typhoon can disrupt coastal infrastructure through swell even without landfall.

claims.text: The fourth official report added an upbound closure from Oiso-nishi IC to Seisho-Ninomiya IC, about 2.3 km, while the roughly 6.0 km downbound closure from Oiso-higashi IC to Seisho-Ninomiya IC continued.
claims.basis: Joint fourth report from MLIT Yokohama National Highway Office and NEXCO Central Japan.

claims.text: The same report lists Seisho-Ninomiya IC to Odawara-nishi IC, about 13.4 km, and Hayakawa JCT to Ishibashi IC, about 1.6 km, closed in both directions.
Authorities say reopening will occur only after high waves subside and safety is confirmed.
At 10:00 p.m. on October 6, TV Kanagawa still reported the expanded closure pattern in force.
The fourth report makes the earlier closure map stale for drivers because an additional upbound free-section segment was added after the previous official update.
claims.basis: Comparison of the fourth report with the earlier ALAM version.

claims.text: Do not assume the whole Seisho Bypass is closed, that the restrictions will last all day on October 7, or that Typhoon 27 must make landfall for these impacts to occur.
claims.basis: The sources identify specific closed sections and conditional reopening, not those broader outcomes.

change_summary.previous: ALAM's prior version reflected the third official report: the original roughly 6 km downbound closure continued and toll-road sections were closed in both directions.
change_summary.now: The fourth report added a new roughly 2.3 km upbound closure from Oiso-nishi IC to Seisho-Ninomiya IC. The existing downbound and toll-road closures continued, and TV Kanagawa still reported this expanded pattern at 10:00 p.m. October 6.
change_summary.why_change_matters: Anyone relying on the earlier map could incorrectly assume this upbound free-section segment remained available. The update materially changes route planning.

content.whats_new: May additional upbound restriction na: Oiso-nishi IC to Seisho-Ninomiya IC, about 2.3 km. The earlier downbound and toll-road restrictions remained in the fourth official report.
content.skeptical_view: This is a road-status update, not evidence that all of Kanagawa is facing severe typhoon damage. The verified signal is specific: high waves caused overtopping and progressively broader Seisho Bypass restrictions.
content.what_next: Check official live road information immediately before departure. The agencies say reopening depends on the waves subsiding and completion of safety checks.
content.what_would_change_mind: A formal final/reopening notice, another change in the closed sections, or materially different official wave guidance would change this assessment.
content.recommendation: If you need the Shonan–Odawara coastal corridor this morning, huwag umasa sa yesterday morning's route map. Check the latest official traffic status before leaving and be ready to reroute.
